title: Cliff's groups at Cafe Society and Wellman Braud
summary: They discuss Village Cats-era recordings and whether Wellman Braud was from Washington.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, some are with a group called the Village Cats.

That would be presumably when he was at Cafe Society.

Could be, could be, yeah, it must be because he must have gone into Cafe Society about 1941. But this is not -- I'm not sure that these guys played -- it doesn't seem to me that these guys were at Cafe Society at the time. They were probably just a bunch of guys that got together and made this tape.
Yeah, Gene Cedric was with Fats Waller (Unintelligible)

That's right and Edward Barksdale on Guitar, Sidney Bechet, but I think Sidney was with Cafe Society for a while and so did Sidney de Paris and Wilbur de Paris and Wellman Braud on bass and Eddie Dougherty on drums.
Was Wellman Braud from Washington also because he was an early Ellingtonian.
I don't think that Wellman Braud was from Washington. I have some friends from Homestead -- in fact some very dear friends of

mine. One of the Braudeses there was married to Wellman Braud and from what I could understand, he was from New York? I'm not sure, and these records, Charlie Howze brought up when we had the dedication on the House that Jazz Built.
I don't have most of the things that Cliff did, but I do have that tape that Ed Beach -- I took it off the air.
And some other material we talked about on the wire recorder.
Oh, yes, on the wire recorder. I don't know when I'm ever going to get a chance to hear that.

I see by your notes here, I've mentioned earlier that it was around 1926 that Cliff came to New York, but I see it was 1923 and when he came in 1923, he joined Lionel Howard's Musical Aces and also around 1925 he accompanied singers like Viola McCoy, Lena Wilson, Clara Smith and Sarah-- I don't know who this person is --
*According to John Chilton's Who's Who in Jazz, Braud was born in St. James Parish, Louisiana.
